summary.text: Jon Cardin is a Democratic delegate representing District 11B in the Maryland House of Delegates and is seeking re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election.
An attorney, he previously served in the House of Delegates from 2003 to 2015 and returned in 2019.

paragraphs.text: Jon Cardin was born in Baltimore, Maryland.

He earned a bachelor's degree in international relations from Tufts University in 1992, master's degrees in policy sciences from the University of Maryland, Baltimore County and in Judaic studies from Baltimore Hebrew University in 1996, and a juris doctor from the University of Maryland in 2001.

His career experience includes work as an attorney, as a Spanish teacher and lacrosse and basketball coach at Mercersburg Academy, and as a law clerk to Judge William D. Quarles, Jr., of the Baltimore City Circuit Court.
He has served as vice chairman of the American Council of Young Political Leaders and as executive director of the Project Judaica Foundation.
Cardin represented Maryland House of Delegates District 11 from 2003 to 2015 and has held his current seat since 2019.
He serves on the Judiciary Committee.
